12 A fairground ride consists of four carriages connected to a central vertical pole, as shown in the
following view from above.

A motor rotates the central pole about its axis. This results in the four carriages each moving
along a circular path.
The distance from the middle of each carriage to the centre of the pole is 3.20 m. When they are
moving, each carriage experiences an air resistance force of 85.0 N. Assume that there are no
other significant resistive forces.
Which torque does the motor need to apply to the pole to keep the system rotating at constant
maximum speed?
A
5.44 N m
B
272 N m
C
544 N m
D
1090 N m

hints: Notice each of the four carriages has an $85.0 \text{ N}$ air resistance force acting tangentially opposite the direction of rotation at radius $3.20 \text{ m}$.
Recall torque is force times perpendicular distance from the pivot, so calculate $85.0 \text{ N} \times 3.20 \text{ m}$ for one carriage.
For constant maximum speed the motor torque must balance the sum of all four resistive torques, so multiply the one-carriage torque by 4.
walkthrough: At constant speed there is no resultant torque, so motor torque must equal total resistive torque from air resistance.
For one carriage, the air resistance acts tangentially, perpendicular to the $3.20 \text{ m}$ arm from the pole, so torque $= Fd$.
Substitute values with units: $T_1 = 85.0 \text{ N} \times 3.20 \text{ m} = 272 \text{ N m}$ for one carriage.
There are four identical carriages, so total resistive torque $= 4 \times 272 \text{ N m} = 1088 \text{ N m}$.
Rounded to three significant figures this is about $1090 \text{ N m}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: About $5.44 \text{ N m}$ is far too small and does not match $F \times d$ for the given $85.0 \text{ N}$ and $3.20 \text{ m}$.

B.explanation: About $272 \text{ N m}$ is the resistive torque from one carriage only, since $85.0 \times 3.20 = 272$.

C.explanation: About $544 \text{ N m}$ is the resistive torque from two carriages only, so it misses half the total resistance.

D.explanation: Total resistive torque is $4 \times 85.0 \times 3.20 = 1088 \text{ N m}$, about $1090 \text{ N m}$, which the motor must balance.
